newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Global bulls help Taiwan stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Global bulls help Taiwan stocks to higher close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Saturday, thanks to a big bull run in the U.S. and European markets, but brokers warned that short-term profit-taking could soon emerge.
The index finished at a two-month high of 8,502.18, a gain of 187.16 points or 2.25 percent compared to Friday.
Turnover was a relatively active T$111.6 billion in the abbreviated Saturday session.
Taking momentum from the dramatic overseas stock rallies, Taiwan's heavily weighted financials soared 5.84 percent.

U.S. stocks capped a record-breaking week on Friday with the Dow Jones industrial average jumping 70.57 points to 7,782.04, its sixth consecutive record close. The British and German markets also surged on Friday to record finishes.
In Taiwan, Saturday's closing level was the highest since its April 29 finish of 8,592.44 and came within 160 points of a seven-year high 8,661.72 set on April 26.
Since that peak, the island's bourse, which had risen more than 25 percent in early 1997, has endured a modest correction.
Brokers said it was still too early to say whether the market was returning to its bullish ways.
"The heavily weighted financial sector can easily boost share prices, but a sustainable gain will require rises in the trendsetting electronics sector," National Securities' analyst Allen Huang.
Electronics, seen as Taiwan's most promising sector, rose only a scant 0.80 percent as many high-tech shares were mired in profit-taking correction against a dramatic recent rise.
Leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor lost 50 cents to T$95.5, unable to sustain the week's dazzling gains.
"The market has reason to stay bullish in the medium term" but faces near-term profit-taking pressure, Huang said.
